feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. This is the final iteration, and the candidate is the iteration 10 design, which is the best raced result (81.25, up from 75.97 in iterations 1 and 6). Its kd 0.25 is the only change from the iteration 1 baseline. Across the kd sweep, s-bend progress was 0.155 at kd 0.1 (iteration 2), 0.155 at kd 0.15 (iteration 7), 0.29 at kd 0.2 (iterations 1 and 6), and 0.276 at kd 0.25 (iteration 10). Iteration 10 also lowered steering_oscillation on the s-bend from 0.23 to 0.21 and raised oval progress from 0.16 to 0.21. The candidate is valid: every field is inside its contract limits, and five sensors match five weights. Every other lever tested lowered the score: base_speed 1.2 and 1.5 (iterations 2 and 8), kp 2.5 (iteration 3), wider spacing (iteration 4), and sensor_size 0.016 (iteration 5). max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 under all of them, so the off-track failure is not fixed by anything tested. With no further race in the team's budget, the best-supported design is the one already raced, and an untested change would add risk on the unseen track. Approve it unchanged.
requested_changes: Keep kp 2.0, ki 0.0, base_speed 1.4, kd 0.25, and last_direction line loss exactly as raced in iteration 10. Changing any of these would be untested on the held-back track.

Keep the sensor geometry at x -0.02..0.02, y 0.04 and sensor_size 0.012. Iterations 4 and 5 showed that wider spacing and the 0.016 footprint both cut s-bend and oval progress without moving max_error.
Do not raise kd to 0.3 in this final design. The s-bend trend flattened between kd 0.2 (0.29) and kd 0.25 (0.276), so the progress peak is probably near 0.2 to 0.25, and kd 0.3 is an untested risk.
